metadata.note: The Greenwich and Johnsonville (Union Village and Johnsonville Railroad 1866; Greenwich and Johnsonville Railroad 1874; Railway 1879; consolidated with the Battenkill Railroad 1903), a Washington County, NY short line: Johnsonville (junction with the Troy & Boston, later Fitchburg / Boston and Maine) - Greenwich, 14 mi, opened 1870, plus a c.10.1 mi branch Greenwich - Greenwich Junction (D&H Washington Branch, near Salem) built c.1907 and a 7 mi extension Greenwich - Thomson - Schuylerville opened 1903. The D&H bought its stock in 1906 but it remained a separately named carrier and Official Guide entry. Johnsonville - Greenwich abandoned July 1932; the rest became freight-only and passed to the Batten Kill Railroad in 1982. Research report: research/branches/greenwich_and_johnsonville_railway.txt.

metadata.operator_split: None. The D&H bought the G&J's capital stock in 1906 (WP, RF; WP-BK says 'around 1900' - conflict), but the G&J kept its own name as the carrier in the 1911 and 1927 D&H public timetables (NCS agency 'Greenwich & Johnsonville Railway Company'), in the 1913 B&M ticket notice, and in its own Official Guide entry to 1951. No source names the D&H as operator of G&J passenger trains, so both features stay in the G&J colour (report recommendation, accepted by the map's owner).
metadata.colors: 'Greenwich and Johnsonville Railway' had no colour anywhere in data/ (checked programmatically). #27B93B is new: used by no other feature in data/, chosen as the candidate farthest from all 515 colours in use, and distinct from the neighbouring D&H teal #146B70 and B&M navy #1D3557.
omitted: Schuylerville extension Greenwich - Middle Falls - Thomson - Schuylerville (report block [3], drawable NONE): opened 1903, but no source shows a G&J passenger train on it in any year - not in Fowler's station list nor in the NCS transcriptions of the 1911 and 1927 D&H timetables. The corridor's passenger service was the Greenwich & Schuylerville Electric / Hudson Valley Railway trolley (1895-1928), a different company not drawn here.
Greenwich Junction - Greenwich - Thomson as a freight-only road (report block [4]; G52 'Freight Service' 1951): Rule 1.
Batten Kill Railroad excursions after 1994, ended by late 2003 (report block [5]): no confirmed operating year or route; a separate company if ever drawn.
Batten Kill Railroad freight from 1982: Rule 1.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN: Johnsonville - Greenwich drawn to 1927, the last confirmed passenger year (31 Oct 1927 D&H public timetable via NCS). The real end lies between 1927 and the July 1932 abandonment. Leads: Nestle, 'Rails Along the Battenkill' (1983); Shaughnessy, Delaware & Hudson (1997) p.313; Greenwich Journal and Salem Press (nyshistoricnewspapers.org); D&H public timetables 1928-1932.

OPEN: Salem Branch drawn to 1927, the last confirmed passenger year. Wikipedia's 'passenger service ended in 1933' cites W. A. Cormier's 2015 NY History Review blog post, now offline and not seen - unconfirmed. Freight-only by 1951 (G52).

Salem Branch start: built c.1907 ('completed in 1907', Railfan & Railroad; 'by 1907', WP-BK). Drawn from 1913 on INDIRECT evidence only (B&M mileage tickets good 'between all stations' of the G&J, Jan 1913); the first source naming the route is the 1927 D&H timetable. Passenger service 1907-1912 is unconfirmed, and absence from the NCS transcription of the June 1911 timetable is not evidence either way.

Schuylerville extension (1903 - early 1930s): whether the G&J ever ran passenger trains Greenwich - Thomson - Schuylerville is not found either way; not drawn. 1910 PSC Reports of Decisions p.92 and Nestle (1983) are the leads. Opening year conflict: 1903 (WP, RF) vs Hudson bridge 'built 1901' (PedalPoint).
NCS evidence is second-hand: the 1911 and 1927 D&H public timetables themselves were not seen.
Headways and speeds on both features are estimates; no timetable times seen.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 14.1 mi against 14 mi documented (ICC abandonment 'Johnsonville to Greenwich, N. Y., 14 miles', Washington Times 5 Jul 1932; Wikipedia 14 mi) and 15 mi by Fowler's mileposts = +0.7% vs 14 mi. No straight-line leg longer than a few hundred metres: 100% of the route-mileage on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=D&H and named or located as the former G&J Johnsonville line (ways 48887817-48887819, 1428364320/1, 48887816, 32742462, 1328262773-80, 1428364024/5/55/56, 32742364, 980948974-83, 32742212, 20644917 'Eddy Street', 48887825, 188546505, 1428363736, 159043469/70 'former G&J Johnsonville Branch'). The rail was lifted in 1932 and from about South Cambridge to the south edge of Greenwich village (c.9 mi) the OSM abandoned-railway ways are the same ways as Washington County Route 74 (highway=tertiary, name 'County Road 74'), which was built on the grade: so that stretch follows the road that occupies the grade, not an independently surveyed railway line, and is good to the width of the road wherever the road kept to the grade. Johnsonville end: the trace's first vertex snapped c.0.2 mi north of the BHT&W/B&M Johnsonville vertex (-73.514291, 42.915327, the cut point in boston_hoosac_tunnel_and_western_railway.geojson); that c.0.18 mi is a short straight connector chord (approximated) drawn to meet the existing line rather than redrawing it. Greenwich end: ends on the Batten Kill (ex-G&J) track at the west end of the Greenwich yard (-73.499049, 43.086347), the same vertex the Salem Branch feature starts from. Milepost check against Fowler (miles from Greenwich, Fowler/traced, to the nearest vertex of each hamlet's OSM place node): South Cambridge 10/9.3, West Cambridge 8/7.9, Vly Summit 7/6.0, Archdale 5/4.6. Lee's and Easton were not used as waypoints (Nominatim returned a street and nothing respectively). Alignment: the line's own grade, never relocated as far as known; there is no later alignment to confuse with it.

segments.note: Report block [1]. Opened 31 Aug 1870 (Wikipedia, citing Shaughnessy, Delaware & Hudson, 1997, p.219); 'The Greenwich and Johnsonville Railroad is completed' (Rutland Weekly Herald 4 Aug 1870). The Town of Greenwich's '1869' is taken as the construction year. Steam from opening - no animal traction (Rule 5). Passenger evidence: Greenwich, Johnsonville and intermediate stations in the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler); passengers aboard a G&J train into Greenwich, Bennington Evening Banner 4 Aug 1906; Boston & Maine mileage tickets honoured 'between all stations' of the G&J, Bennington Evening Banner 3 Jan 1913; route Greenwich - Johnsonville in the D&H public timetables of 25 Jun 1911 and 31 Oct 1927 (Nashua City Station transcription, timetables themselves not seen). D&H bought the G&J's stock in 1906 but the G&J stayed the named carrier in those timetables and ticket notices, so no Rule 4 split. END YEAR: 1927 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year (31 Oct 1927 D&H timetable), NOT a known end - service ran some unknown time past it, and certainly no later than the ICC-authorised abandonment of Johnsonville - Greenwich (Washington Times 5 Jul 1932; effective 28 Jul 1932 per Wikipedia/Shaughnessy p.313), after which the track was lifted. Bracket 1927-1932. Wikipedia's 'passenger service ended in 1933' cannot apply to this line, gone in 1932. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 480 (about two or three trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE - no timetable times seen.
sources: Segment-level: start - Wikipedia citing Shaughnessy p.219 (31 Aug 1870), Rutland Weekly Herald 4 Aug 1870 p.3; service - Fowler (1875 Official Guide), Bennington Evening Banner 4 Aug 1906 p.1 and 3 Jan 1913 p.1, Nashua City Station transcription of D&H public timetables 25 Jun 1911 and 31 Oct 1927 (end = last confirmed year); ceiling - Washington Times 5 Jul 1932 p.19 (ICC abandonment). Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Report block [2]. Built under D&H control to tie the G&J into the D&H Washington Branch at Greenwich Junction, just south of Salem: 'completed in 1907, financed by D&H' (Railfan & Railroad, Oct 2022); built 'by 1907' (Wikipedia, Batten Kill Railroad). START YEAR: 1913 is INDIRECT evidence, not the opening - the Boston & Maine mileage-ticket notice of Jan 1913 says the tickets are good 'between all stations' of the G&J (Bennington Evening Banner 3 Jan 1913), which would include this branch's stations, but does not name it. The branch was built c.1907; no passenger train on it is confirmed for 1907-1912 (it is not in the NCS transcription of the June 1911 D&H timetable - absence, recorded only). The first source that names the route is the D&H public timetable of 31 Oct 1927 (route Greenwich - Greenwich Junction: Battenville, Center Falls, East Greenwich; Nashua City Station transcription). A strict reading would draw 1927 only. END YEAR: 1927 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, NOT a known end. Wikipedia says 'passenger service ended in 1933', citing a 2015 blog post (now offline, not seen) - unconfirmed; after July 1932 this branch was the G&J's only outlet, so 1933 is plausible. By the Feb 1952 Official Guide it was 'Freight Service' only (East Greenwich and Greenwich Junction daggered for freight), which dates the end only to 'before 1951'. Bracket 1907-1933. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued under the D&H to the 15 Nov 1981 embargo and under the Batten Kill Railroad from 1982 (context, not drawn). headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE - no timetable times seen.
sources: Segment-level: start - Bennington Evening Banner 3 Jan 1913 p.1 (mileage tickets 'between all stations'; indirect), construction c.1907 from Railfan & Railroad Oct 2022 and Wikipedia (Batten Kill Railroad); end - Nashua City Station transcription of the D&H public timetable of 31 Oct 1927 (last confirmed year); Wikipedia's 1933 end unconfirmed. Headway not sourced (estimate).
